analysis_unit: One run (one protocol execution from one runner node) is one sample; attempts inside a run are samples within a run, never independent observations (ADR-0003).

claims.name: latency_distribution
claims.question: Client-observed time-to-first-token and total-latency distributions for the target under the fixed prompt set, concurrency, and max_tokens.

derivation.per_run: nearest-rank percentiles (p50, p90, p95, p99) over succeeded attempts only
derivation.across_runs: distribution of per-run percentiles across compatible runs; report the spread, never a single pooled number

excludes: runs with execution_status excluded or unobserved

claims.name: error_rate
claims.question: Fraction of attempts the target failed under the protocol.

derivation.source: result.summary.failed / result.summary.attempted, with result.summary.error_classes for the breakdown
derivation.across_runs: distribution of per-run rates across compatible runs

excludes: unobserved attempts (target unreachable before any attempt) are never counted as failures (R4)

cost_model.description: Estimated spend for one plan of `planned` sequential chat completions. Fixture targets (the in-repo stub server) bill nothing; a real endpoint is priced from operator-supplied per-token prices, because the pack cannot know a provider's price list.
notes: prompt_tokens_per_request is an upper bound over harness/prompts.json plus the system prompt.
max_tokens is the per-request completion cap the runner passes in input.json (budget.max_tokens); the estimate assumes every request returns the cap, so it is an upper bound.
Without both operator prices a non-fixture target has no estimate and the runner refuses to execute (fail closed, ADR-0003).
